title: 一些科技股正在暴跌——这对人工智能革命意味着什么？
content: Image source,AFP via Getty ImagesBySimon JackBusiness editorPublished29 July 2026, 14:49 BSTUpdated 28 minutes agoSharp falls in the value of chip makers have stoked investor concerns that the euphoria around artificial intelligence (AI) related companies is fading.The AI revolution has promised to revolutionise the way we work and live and has created vast wealth for investors in a handful of companies predominantly in the US and Asia.Companies are desperate to be the winners of a transformative technology that many have compared to the advent of the internet, the telephone, even electricity itself.As Sir Demis Hassabis, founder of UK company Deepmind, which was eventually bought a decade ago by US giant Google, has commented that Artificial Intelligence "cannot be compared to standard technological breakthroughs, not even ones as consequential as the internet or mobile. It is much more akin to the discovery of electricity or fire."Referring to the fact that many chips are made of silicon, which is essentially sand, he added "we've essentially found a way to make sand think. It's miraculous."The euphoria for this technology has boosted the value of some world's biggest companies even as they spend hundreds of billions of dollars on the building blocks of the technology.But over the last few weeks, the value of some of the companies that make those building blocks has plummetted - prompting some to question whether what some have dubbed "the AI bubble" is about to burst.Some of the sharpest falls have been in Asia, with shares in Korean chip makers such as SK Hynix and Samsung down 46% and 35% respectively over the last month as investors worry the recent boom in demand for the chips that power AI is unsustainable.Yet these shares still are up threefold and fivefold respectively over the last year, leading many to conclude that some caution and profit taking after such massive gains was inevitable â and indeed healthy.The South Korean stock market is notoriously volatile, but concerns have spilled over into the big US companies.Shares in Google and Tesla plunged briefly before recovering last week after both firms pledged to spend billions more on AI in the months and years to come despite so far it losing them money.And with other big names such as Meta, Microsoft and Amazon reporting their latest financial results this week, investors have the opportunity to scrutinise just how much these companies are now betting on AI."There is still a healthy degree of scepticism about the ability of these investments to generate a commensurate level of return," Russ Mould, an investment director at AJ Bell, said.But according to leading tech investor Eileen Burbidge despite the concerns there's not yet a serious reckoning."The AI bubble hasn't burst but it's letting out air," she told the BBC.China breakthroughOne of the other triggers for the concerns has been a reported breakthrough in the manufacturing process by a Chinese company, potentially making China more self-sufficient in chip design and production.That has added to lingering concerns that the big AI companies â Meta, Alphabet, Open AI, Anthropic â will find it hard to charge end users enough to justify the hundreds of billions being spent on buying the chips and building the data centres that power the technology.As a result, firms that have announced big increases in spending on AI have not always been welcomed with the same enthusiasm by investors.For example, SpaceX â which is predominantly an AI company - has seen its shares fall 14% from its much-hyped debut on the stock market and nearly 50% from its peak in June.Apple â which has largely sat out the AI arms race â has seen its shares rise 21% over the last month to reclaim its title as the world's most valuable company from chip maker Nvidia.Meanwhile London's benchmark FTSE 100 index which have some have dubbed the "anti-tech index", briefly touched a record high - one of the few periods in recent years where it has benefited from not being tech-heavy.Growing concernsHistorically it is possible for investors to lose money even if the technology they are backing succeeds.For example, while railways transformed economies â particularly in the US â plenty of people lost money along the way. Unlike rail tracks â which once built are good for decades â data centres are likely to need upgrading frequently to include the latest and fastest processors.Add to that lot, concerns that some of the big AI companies have taken big stakes or lent money to each other leading to circular funding that means that any potential failures could have a damaging impact on the fortunes of others.There is also increasing cultural opposition to the build out and adoption of AI.A growing number of national, state or local governments are pausing, banning or restricting new data centre construction on environmental grounds thanks to their vast water and energy needs.Meanwhile, high profile AI advocates have found themselves booed by students who fear that AI will replace many graduate level jobs.Despite all of that, Eileen Burbidge is still positive. "I see the glass half full - if you bought shares in chip makers a year ago you are feeling pretty good right now."But there is no doubt that investors are watching companies plans for spending and their projections for when they get paid back with post euphoric scrutiny.Related topicsArtificial intelligenceMore on this storyChip stocks slide in US and Asia as AI jitters rattle investorsPublished1 day agoWorld's largest chipmaker does not rule out price rises as costs increasePublished9 JuneChinese chipmaker shares surge nearly 470% in blockbuster stock market debutPublished2 days ago

title: Humana 超出季度预期，由于医疗成本保持不变，维持利润前景
content:
Humanaon 周三公布的第二季度业绩超出预期，因为这家健康保险公司在医疗服务方面的支出符合预期。

该公司还维持了 2026 年调整后每股收益至少 9 美元的预期。

Humana 首席财务官 Celeste Mellet 在接受采访时表示，盈利超出预期是由 Humana 保险业务和 CenterWell 医疗服务部门的实力推动的。她表示，医疗和药品成本趋势符合 Humana 对新会员和现有会员的预期。她补充说，该公司认为住院领域的医疗成本“略有优惠”，特别是在接受基于价值的提供商的护理的会员中。

尽管如此，坎托·菲茨杰拉德(Cantor Fitzgerald)分析师在周三的一份报告中称，在最近的盈利超出预期以及监管私营医疗保险优势计划的其他保险公司上调指导后，利润前景不变令人“失望”。随着一些公司提高前景并更好地应对这些计划中不断上涨的医疗成本，投资者一直在提高对该行业的预期——这个问题已经困扰整个行业两年多了。

尽管季度表现强劲，Humana 股价周三仍下跌超过 6%。该公司是最大的 Medicare Advantage 提供商之一，为 65 岁及以上的人和残疾人提供服务。

根据 LSEG 对分析师的调查，该公司第二季度的报告与华尔街的预期相比如下：

该公司公布的第二季度净利润为 6.94 亿美元，即每股 5.73 美元，而去年同期净利润为 5.45 亿美元，即每股 4.51 美元。一年前的一段时期。不包括摊销和减值费用等项目，Humana 每股盈利 7.61 美元。

收入从上年同期的 323.9 亿美元攀升至 408.7 亿美元。根据 StreetAccount 的数据，该公司的保险公司和 Centerwell 部门本季度的销售预期均超过分析师的预期。

保险公司，尤其是那些运行 Medicare Advantage 计划的保险公司，因大量寻求医疗服务的人而受到挤压，他们推迟了大流行后和 GLP-1 等高成本特殊药物等因素。

但 Humana 的医疗福利比率（衡量支付的总医疗费用相对于收取的保费的衡量标准）为第二季度为91.2%，符合分析师预期。 Mellet 表示，该比率也符合公司对本季度新会员和现有会员的预期。

Mellet 表示：“我认为，这是[医疗成本]趋势稳定与我们为帮助我们的会员和患者带来更好的健康结果而采取的行动相结合的结果。”

不过，该比率仍略高于去年同期报告的 89.9%。较低的比率通常表明该公司收取的保费多于支付的福利，从而带来更高的盈利能力。

Mellet 表示，明年的医疗成本预期“相当一致”。该公司正在观察今年住院人数等服务是否会继续下降，但她表示，“目前，我们认为医疗成本更加稳定。”

与此同时，梅莱特指出，在药品价格和新药推出的推动下，药房医疗成本趋势仍然“非常高”。她表示，与 2026 年相比，明年的成本将略高，但补充说，这是一个更广泛的药品成本问题，而不是会员需求的问题。

Mellet 表示，Humana 预计 2027 年 Medicare Advantage 计划的变化将有助于提高盈利能力，并使公司有望在 2028 年之前实现至少 3% 的可持续税前利润率。她表示，该保险公司还对其通过扩大会员、提高质量来提高收入的能力充满信心。对其 Medicare Advantage 计划进行评级，维持定价纪律并控制成本。

title: 国际足联卷入了价值 200 亿美元的世界杯争议。这是发生的事情
content:
世界杯正式出售——至少是其中的一部分。世界足球管理机构国际足联周二宣布，计划成立一家子公司来运营这项赛事，这为投资者购买这家分拆公司最多 20% 的股份打开了大门。

在国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺 (Gianni Infantino) 的精心策划下，此举在整个足球界引起了强烈反对。欧洲足球管理机构欧足联指责国际足联“越界”，并表示赛事不是为了出售。

CNBC 探讨了国际足联的计划以及为何该提议在足球界如此不受欢迎。

受到有史以来规模最大、商业上最成功的世界杯的鼓舞，因凡蒂诺正在通过新企业 FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE) 推动更大的商业化。

在周二，FIFA 表示，FFE 将从第三方筹集至多 42 亿美元，这家子公司的估值为 200 亿美元。该组织补充说，它将保留对该合资企业的最终控制权。

“游戏的某些部分已将这种受欢迎程度转化为显着的商业价值 - 我们庆祝这一成功，并希望它能够继续下去，因为它提升了整个游戏，”因凡蒂诺在声明中表示。

“...我们的下一阶段增长需要为此构建一个结构，在这个结构中，游戏的商业部分作为一个专注、专注的业务运营，其价值在全世界范围内更多更好地共享，”他批评者认为，允许私人投资者影响足球这项最负盛名的国际赛事，可能会让他们对这项运动的运作方式产生不适当的影响。

该提案重新点燃了国际足联和欧足联之间的激烈竞争。

“足球的灵魂和治理不是可以交易的资产，尤其是在谁获得经济利益的透明度为零的情况下，”欧足联在一份声明中表示。 “我们都不是足球的所有者。这不是国际足联可以出售的。”

在周三发布的另一份声明中，欧足联补充道：

“国际足联不能继续利用我们的运动来丰富自己和他们的朋友。我们可以正确地发展这项运动。现在是时候优先考虑协会、俱乐部、联赛、球员和球迷了。”

英国新任首相安迪·伯纳姆也介入其中，在 X 上写道，世界杯“不是产品”。

因凡蒂诺与唐纳德·特朗普总统的密切关系已广为人知，并在世界杯期间受到密切关注。

这笔交易得到了约书亚·库什纳的 Thrive Capital 的支持，他的兄弟贾里德是特朗普的女婿。

J.P.国际足联补充说，摩根也已受聘管理该交易。

要获得批准，该计划需要获得 211 名成员中的大多数以及国际足联 37 名成员的理事会的批准。据报道，欧足联及其欧洲选民正在考虑抵制世界杯，代表了一小部分有影响力的国家。

国际足联作为非营利组织的地位意味着其资金将被重新分配用于在这些国家建设足球基础设施。因凡蒂诺计划向其成员提供高达 2000 万美元一次性资本的机会，这可能会给他在寻求通过该法案时带来优势。

但每个成员也拥有投票权，这在管理机构及其底层参与者之间建立了一种循环关系。

“因凡蒂诺领导下的国际足联向小国家提供了大量资金，这些国家反过来投票支持他连任主席，”足球金融教授基兰·马奎尔告诉记者。上周 CNBC。

title: 数据中心可以支付数亿美元的电力需求押金
content: 图片来源，彭博社来自 Getty Images 图片说明，英国目前有 564 个数据中心，作者：Laura CressTechnology 记者 2026 年 7 月 29 日发布，英国夏令时间 10:50 于 4 小时前更新 Ofgem 提出了新措施，可能会让数据中心开发商预先支付数亿英镑。英国能源监管机构表示，在日益增加的情况下，对于想要连接到网络的项目应该收取可退还的费用它建议开发商为每兆瓦支付 237,500 英镑至 712,500 英镑的押金，这意味着寻求 1 吉瓦 (GW) 电力的数据中心必须预先支付数亿美元，如果项目完成，则需要偿还。这项提议是在该国部分地区对新数据中心计划日益反对的情况下进行的，而新数据中心是为人工智能热潮提供动力所需的。数据中心是大型建筑，里面装有用于存储和处理数据的计算机服务器， Ofgem已开始就其提案进行磋商，该磋商将持续到9月16日。它表示，过去一年中寻求并网的项目所要求的电力容量已从41吉瓦增加到125吉瓦，反映出需求的急剧增长。这比2025年英国约46吉瓦的峰值电力需求高出一倍多。监管机构表示，这些项目必须达到关键里程碑才能保持其在电网中的地位连接队列，需求激增。近年来，世界各地建立了越来越多的数据中心，提供训练和运行人工智能系统所需的计算能力。但它们存在争议，尤其是对居住在这些数据中心附近的人们而言。居民对噪音、电力需求以及有时用于冷却产生大量热量的高性能芯片的大量水提出了担忧。根据数据中心地图外部，目前英国列出了 564 个数据中心。尤其是苏格兰被视为由于提供可再生能源为中心供电，因此为未来项目提供了良好的位置，目前有 24 个项目正在规划过程中。Ofgem 表示，这些计划旨在解决“投机性项目，即在没有任何明确连接意图的情况下确保稀缺网络容量的项目”。该监管机构能源系统设计和开发总监埃莉诺·沃伯顿 (Eleanor Warburton) 表示：“英国的电力需求连接队列规模在不到一年的时间里增加了两倍多，消费者不应该承担由此产生的风险能源安全和净零部能源部长 Michael Shanks 表示，他相信 Ofgem 的行动将“有助于确保可行的连接就绪项目能够启动，而不会受到投机性应用的阻碍”。“英国需要一个适合 21 世纪的电网连接系统，允许企业投资和增长，在全国范围内创造就业机会，”他说。“我不能喝水”——美国数据旁边的生活中心发布2025年7月10日为什么成千上万的人反对建立新的数据中心？发布7月9日随着担忧的增加，数据中心将在英国各地扩展发布2025年8月15日订阅我们的Tech Decoded时事通讯以跟踪世界顶级技术故事和趋势。在英国以外？在此注册。相关主题宝石能源行业人工智能

title: 随着利润的增长，抹茶和蛋白质为格雷格斯带来了回报
content: 图片来源，iStock社论/Getty Images 图片说明，Greggs推出一系列新产品后利润上涨 作者：Emer Moreau商业记者 5小时前发布Greggs转向更健康的产品和流行饮料，帮助其提高了销量，这家面包连锁店报告称，今年上半年利润增长了20%。 英国最大的快餐连锁店Greggs今年推出了一系列新产品，其中许多产品锁定了Greggs 首席执行官 Roisin Currie 此前告诉 BBC 新闻，减肥药的兴起导致顾客开始寻找“小份量”，这可能会影响其盈利。截至 6 月底的 26 周内，面包店总销售额突破 11 亿英镑，比去年同期高出 7.2%。上半年税前利润为 7600 万英镑- 高于 2025 年前六个月的 6350 万英镑。Currie 表示，该公司正在“根据不断变化的口味和趋势扩大和创新我们的菜单”。该公司于 5 月重新推出了沙拉系列，“添加蛋白质并为顾客提供更多选择”。该公司还试图通过其新冰抹茶拿铁来吸引“新的和年轻的顾客”，并通过使标签上的营养信息更加清晰来吸引注重健康的消费者。英国的门店数量比麦当劳还多，2026 年上半年新开了 34 家门店。考虑到 31 家门店关闭，总数达到 2,773 家。超过一半的新店位于一英里内没有 Greggs 门店的地区。报告称，在远离高街的地区，包括汽油前院、超市、零售公园、医院和大学校园，也有类似比例的新店开业。Currie 表示，Greggs 正在监控顾客行为，以了解更多信息。确保新店“在不蚕食现有商店销售的情况下”增加客流量。她还表示，继去年多次涨价之后，格雷格斯的早餐、午餐和“大”优惠在五月份上涨后，没有涨价计划。“我们的价格处于一个良好的位置，我们现在将努力保护消费者，并确保我们能够在今年剩下的时间里提供这种价值，”她说。老板说，减肥针影响了格雷格斯，1月8日出版Wealth Club 的策略师表示，结果表明，尽管许多消费者变得更加注重健康，“人们仍然对价格实惠的美食有健康的胃口”。“它也证明了它能够灵活地跟上最新的食品趋势，表明它可以与更多的优质咖啡馆竞争。”冰抹茶拿铁已成为其最新菜单改造的热门产品之一，这表明这家面包连锁店可以将社交媒体启发的口味与其标志性的价值产品融合在一起。该公司警告称，除非客户信心得到改善，否则扩大供应链的投资将影响 2026 年剩余时间的利润。BTG Consulting 的执行合伙人朱莉·帕尔默 (Julie Palmer) 表示，事实证明，Greggs 已证明能够抵御“减肥药、低支出和信心以及不断上升的就业和商业成本”。“在经历了夏季的运动、啤酒花园和热浪之后，Greggs 将指望秋季和冬季看到对其热糕点和方便携带产品的需求回升。”扩大产品范围以满足不断变化的食品趋势将是吸引人们重返其庞大门店以实现这一目标的关键。”去年，Currie 回答了有关其快速扩张后是否已达到“Greggs 峰值”的问题，并表示“我们已经走出去……以证明情况并非如此”。该集团的目标是在 2026 年净增约 100 至 110 家新店，并尝试“bitesize”模式和自助服务“Greggs Express”模式。其门店数量可能高达 3,500 家。Greggs 表示，对全年业绩的预期保持不变——2026 年基本税前利润与 2025 年的 1.72 亿英镑水平相似。该连锁店已经表示，新店投资成本上升预计将导致下半年利润同比减少。该公司补充称，目前销售额的 6.9% 来自送货上门。它称这是一个增长的“机会”，并指出客户往往在送货上门上的花费是在商店的三倍。相关主题零售GreggsCompanies更多关于这个故事像Costa这样的咖啡连锁店如何失去抹茶一代发布2025年8月30日Greggs在天气警告中延长商店关闭时间6月26日发布首席执行官表示，为了应对成本压力，Greggs将再次提高价格发布2025年10月1日

title: 瑞银首席执行官表示，人工智能的回调是健康的，但投资者应该注意更大的风险
content:
瑞银集团周三公布第二季度盈利增长，首席执行官塞尔吉奥·埃尔莫蒂警告称，地缘政治波动可能会在未来带来新的阻力。

这家瑞士银行和财富管理巨头三个月期间归属于股东的净利润为 28 亿美元，与分析师在 LSEG 编制的共识调查中的预测一致。

税前利润达到 3.6 美元三个月内实现了 10 亿美元的收入，同比增长 64%。

在接受 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目采访时，埃尔莫蒂强调了第二季度整个业务的强劲势头，投资银行、并购和资本市场的渠道“非常好”，杠杆资本市场、债务资本市场和股票也取得了积极的成果。

他还指出了 IPO 市场“充满活力”，瑞银参与了多个项目。交易，包括 SpaceX 具有里程碑意义的首次亮相。该银行还公布了一项新的 30 亿美元股票回购计划，首先在未来三个月内回购 10 亿美元股票。

瑞银股价在早盘交易中上涨了 2.5%。

埃尔莫蒂承认地缘政治裂痕仍然是市场的一个压力点，但对围绕人工智能叙事的潜在日益增长的市场疲劳不以为然。

“显然，我们看到的来自地缘政治方面的持续波动可能会产生一些影响。这是暂时的逆风，”他告诉 CNBC 的卡罗琳·罗斯 (Carolin Roth)。 “但势头良好 - 我们处于有利位置，可以从中受益。”

在人工智能方面，埃尔莫蒂表示，考虑到过去三到四个月市值增长的速度和范围以及集中度，预计会出现调整。

“看到这一点是健康的。我们建议客户在这种情况下始终真正实现多元化，”埃尔莫蒂说。

他说人工智能及其支持基础设施将继续仍然是市场中的“重要因素”，并补充说人工智能的经济影响和效益将在当前集中度之外的许多其他领域发挥作用。

“这是我们可以为客户提供多元化和未来投资的巨大机会。”

title: 乌克兰发现俄罗斯战时经济新压力点
content:
Ukraine's drone attacks onRussia's biggest online retailer Wildberrieshave ratcheted up the pressure on Moscow's wartime economy, with Kyiv seeking to force PresidentVladimir Putinback to the negotiating table after nearly four-and-a-half years of war.

Ukraine has been targeting major logistics centers, such as Russia'sAmazon-style retail giant, as part of a push to severely disrupt the country's supply chains and increase the financial burden facing Russian banks and businesses.

It marks a significant change in approach for Ukrainian forces, following months of long-range drone strikestargeting Russian energy infrastructure.

Wildberries evacuated a warehouse in the central Russian city of Ryazan on Wednesday morning, the company said, after Ukrainian drones struck several industrial facilities.

The Russian government has acknowledged it may need to prop up Wildberries, ReutersreportedTuesday, citing two unnamed sources, with state-controlled bank VTB expected to play a key role. Russia's Foreign Ministry was not immediately available to comment when contacted by CNBC.

Since Russia launched itsfull-scale invasionof Ukraine in early 2022, Russian businesses have faced numerous disruptions due to the war, according to Natalya Kovaleva, a researcher in the Russia and Eurasia program at Chatham House.

"Western sanctions fractured supply chains. Tax increases squeezed margins. Internet blackouts disrupted operations. And recent fuel shortages drove up costs while adding to inflationary pressures," KovalevasaidTuesday in an online post.

"Russia's business owners have largely absorbed these shocks. But Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries present a significant new development, reflecting Kyiv's broader effort to ratchet up economic pressure on business and ordinary Russians."

Kovaleva said Ukraine's hope is that by raising the cost of war for Russian businesses, internal opposition will mount and Putin may be forced to the negotiating table — or at least halt his bombardment of Ukraine's cities.

"It remains to be seen if this strategy will have the desired effect. Even as it becomes even harder to do business in Russia, the country's elites appear more dependent on – and wary of – the Kremlin [than] ever before," Kovaleva said.

Ukrainian PresidentVolodymyr Zelenskyyhas said that warehouses targeted by Ukrainian drones were involved in providing Russian forces with drone components, navigation equipment and other military components.

Wildberries is Russia's biggest online retailer and its equivalent to U.S. e-commerce giant Amazon. Founded in 2004, the company currently employs about 48,000 people.

Alongside Ukrainian attacks on Russian logistics hubs, analysts have warned that Russia's economy is potentially vulnerable to the prospect of sweeping U.S. sanctions.

Zelenskyy said Tuesday that he had discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor production and the importance of reinvigorating the diplomatic process during what he described as a "good meeting" with U.S. PresidentDonald Trumpat the Oval Office.

The meeting took place at a time when the U.S war against Iran and Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine have both reached critical junctures. Trump haspaused airstrikesagainst Iran as part of a push to give diplomacy another chance, while Zelenskyy has been galvanized by a flurry ofdeep-strike successeson Russian territory.

The Trump-Zelenskyy meeting also coincided with a renewed congressional push to tighten sanctions on Moscow, with legislation championed by the lateSen. Lindsey Grahampassing its first Senate hurdle.

"The Russian economy has stalled," Elina Ribakova, senior fellow at Peterson Institute for International Economics, told CNBC's "Europe Early Edition" on Wednesday.

"It will have growth of zero percent this year — at best, we have seen contraction of the economy in the first quarter and industrial output contraction as well. Industrial output contraction means that also the defense sector has decelerated meaningfully. So, Russia is vulnerable."

Ribakova said Russian energy sanctions legislation had the potential to be "extremely impactful" to Putin's wartime economy, particularly at a time when the Russia and Iran conflicts appear to be converging.

Kyiv on Saturdaylaunched an attackon an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, an incident which Tehran said left one sailor dead and injured several others. The Islamic Republic has threatened retaliation over the strike.

"What is giving it a boost is again this connection with Iran," Ribakova said. The fact that Iran is able to close theStrait of Hormuzis boosting oil prices and, of course, giving Russia another way to continue fighting in Ukraine, she added.

title: 指数级盈利增长未能满足人工智能预期，SK 海力士股价暴跌
content:
周三，SK 海力士股价暴跌，原因是第二季度指数级盈利和收入增长未能满足分析师对人工智能宠儿的过高预期。

以下是 SK 海力士第二季度业绩与 LSEG SmartEstimates 的比较，后者根据更一致准确的分析师的预测进行加权：

在盘中早些时候下跌 15% 后，该股周三收盘时收跌 9.6%。该公司在美国上市的股票最新交易价格下跌 3.4%。

该公司的新闻稿显示，截至 6 月份的季度收入同比猛增 257%，营业利润同比飙升近 557%。

与上一季度相比，收入增长 51%，营业利润增长 61%。

该公司表示，由于扩张，需求持续增长。 AI基础设施投资，而AI服务器的高性能产品带动价格上涨，创下新纪录。

公司上半年累计收入首次超过100万亿韩元，凸显了强劲的AI需求。

SK海力士表示，预计今年的资本支出将达到40万亿韩元的高位，并计划在本月早些时候在纳斯达克上市的ADR的基础上再接再厉。

该公司强调它将优先投资增长并努力确保健全的金融结构。它还将继续审查股东回报政策。

展望未来，该公司的目标是利用利川和龙仁的现有制造中心来最大限度地提高产量，同时提高清州的 NAND 产量和先进封装。

eToro 亚太区首席分析师 Josh Gilbert 表示，该公司 83% 的毛利率表明定价能力仍然强劲。他表示：“这种情况并不存在于需求枯竭的市场中，而是存在于客户争夺供应的市场中。”

DRAM 和 NAND 闪存价格均出现环比上涨，该公司通过扩大专注于高附加值产品（包括 HBM、用于 AI 服务器的 DRAM 和企业 SSD）的销售，实现了顶级盈利能力。

在 AI 服务的持续收入和大型科技公司基础设施投资激增的推动下，内存需求增长随着供应需求持续增加，预计这一势头将持续下去。

SK 海力士表示，其 HBM4 已展现出差异化的技术优势，并宣扬其功效和成本竞争力。公司第二季度开始批量出货HBM4，下半年提升产量，上半年也完成HBM4E样品出货。

NAND方面，SK海力士正在加速向先进工艺节点转型，强化大容量高性能产品组合，其中321层产品已占据总产量最大份额，目标年底达到国内产能50%左右。

这家韩国科技巨头生产内存芯片，并为从数据中心到智能手机等消费电子产品的硬件供应零部件，其主要客户包括包括英伟达在内的美国大型企业——最近通过一项价值超过 5000 亿美元的多年交易扩大了合作伙伴关系。

title: 科技股遭遇抛售，软银下跌 7%，AI 股遭受重创
content:
周三，亚洲和欧洲的科技股继续遭遇抛售，半导体股在美国股市再次疲软后领跌。

在韩国，SK 海力士 (SK Hynix) 跌幅超过 15%，收盘下跌 9.61%。该芯片巨头尽管公布了创纪录的季度利润和营收，但未达到分析师预期。

三星电子下跌超过 5%，LG Innotek 下跌 10.89%，首尔半导体下跌 8.89%。

欧洲芯片股也走低。ASML 下跌 3.85%，ASM International 下跌 9.26%，BESI 下跌 3.54%。

最新疲软安本投资公司(Aberdeen Investments)亚洲股票投资总监基伦·潘(Kieron Poon)在周二的一份报告中表示，亚洲芯片股的投资反映了“韩国正在进行的去杠杆化进程以及对全球科技股的疲软情绪”。不过，他补充说，最近的波动“并没有改变我们的长期积极看法。”

日本芯片品牌也出现下跌。日本计算机内存制造商Kioxia下跌13.85%。Tokyo Electronfell下跌10.59%，而通过持有Arm股份的主要人工智能投资代理软银集团下跌6.95%。

全球最大代工芯片制造商台湾台积电下跌3.51%。

中国大陆科技股创业板300指数恒生中国半导体芯片指数上涨 1.43%，而恒生中国半导体芯片指数下跌 2.5%。

隔夜美国半导体股再次疲软，亚洲股市下跌。

英伟达开盘下跌，但收盘持平。英特尔下跌近 6%，AMD 下跌 8%。内存空间名股Micron和Seagate下跌超过8%，Western Digital下跌近7%，Sandisk下跌14%。SK Hynix美国股价下跌 9%。

尽管股价大幅回调，但安本认为此次抛售是一个机会，而不是基本面恶化。 Poon 表示：“最近的市场回调使估值达到更具吸引力的水平，为我们以更合理的价格增加对优质企业的投资创造了机会。”

最近人工智能相关芯片股的回调反映出投资者“回吐了一点人工智能市场的泡沫”，Riedel Research Group 创始人兼总裁 David Riedel 周三向 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Asia”表示。

尽管人们对人工智能融资感到担忧，但他表示，中国竞争的加剧打压了市场情绪，“市场是健康的”，并补充说，存储芯片制造商“不会有什么问题”，但“只是必须回吐一些突然上涨的收益。”

在香港上市的中国互联网股票顶住了整个区域的疲软，截至凌晨 3 点 26 分，腾讯和美团分别上涨了 4.29% 和 2.05%。 ET.阿里巴巴、百度、快手均走高。

title: 由于希思罗机场能够收回跑道项目资金，票价将上涨 15 便士
content: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社凯蒂·奥斯汀交通通讯员发布2026 年 7 月 29 日，英国夏令时 07:18 更新于 1 小时前希思罗机场将被允许向航空公司收取更多服务费用，以收回第三跑道项目早期阶段所花费的资金。航空监管机构允许机场通过提高每位乘客向航空公司收取的机场费用，收回高达 3.2 亿英镑的资金。这最终可能会使 2028 年的机票价格增加 15 便士，并在以后的几年中升至 30 便士。阿罗拉集团 (Arora Group) 的希思罗西机场 (Heathrow West) 提出了涉及较短跑道的竞争设计，但未能成功，该竞标者也将被允许收回 410 万英镑的成本。民航局 (CAA) 和希思罗机场表示，将采取保障措施，保护消费者免受不合理成本的影响。现阶段，收回的成本仅为2025 年和 2026 年跑道的早期规划和设计。实际建造跑道的成本将在机票价格中增加多少还不清楚。CAA 消费者和市场总监蒂姆·约翰逊 (Tim Johnson) 告诉 BBC：“我们已经宣布，可以从乘客那里收回第一笔费用，以帮助规划这一计划。最多可达 3.2 亿英镑。” 希思罗机场还将能够通过增加机场费用来收取希思罗西机场截至去年 11 月的费用。CAA 表示，允许收回这些费用将导致每名乘客的最高机场费用在 2028 年增加约 15 便士，在接下来的几年内预计升至 30 便士。希思罗机场发言人表示：“该项目旨在让旅行更加实惠，为乘客提供更多选择，同时为该国每个地区和国家提供真正的经济增长。”“我们正在仔细考虑。”该发言人补充道，“我们将听取 CAA 的建议，并将做出相应的投资决定。”该发言人补充道。去年 11 月，政府宣布，与阿罗拉的替代计划相比，政府更倾向于机场提出的 330 亿英镑的计划。当时，交通部表示，希思罗机场自己的提议提供了最可行的选择，并且“最有可能”在议会内就规划批准做出决定。CAA 消费者和市场总监蒂姆·约翰逊表示，今天的决定“在支持提供福利之间取得了平衡”监管机构表示，旨在监控成本效率的“保障措施”将包括透明度和成本报告要求以及独立专家的保证。航空公司经常抱怨希思罗机场是世界上最昂贵的枢纽机场，并一再表示担心机场的扩建计划将使其价格更高。政府希望在 2029 年之前做出规划决定。第三条跑道的计划可以追溯到几十年前，与政府合作支持 2003 年的计划。然而，这一想法长期以来也面临气候活动家、许多当地居民和几位政界人士的反对。他们担心额外的跑道会增加空气污染、噪音污染，并违反政府具有法律约束力的气候承诺。联系您对这个故事有任何看法、评论或问题吗？联系表相关主题希思罗机场扩建伦敦希思罗机场更多关于这个故事的希思罗机场“关键”扩建蓝图发布已发布18 6 月政府选择希思罗机场第三跑道更长的计划发布2025 年 11 月 25 日

title: 牛淋浴和风扇如何帮助农民保持牛群凉爽
content: Image caption,Cows at a dairy farm near Chippenham are doused with cool water to beat the heatByDave HarveyWest of England business and environment correspondentPublished4 hours agoDairy farmers are installing "cow showers" and giant cooling fans as hotter, drier summers become more common.Extreme heat has cut milk production by up to 20% and farmers are spending thousands of pounds to keep their cattle cool and protect milk yields.Sarah Godwin's family have invested Â£15,000 in a ventilation and sprinkler system at their farm near Chippenham, Wiltshire, to help their animals cope with the "nearly continuous heatwave we are living through".Professor Nicola Cannon from the Royal Agricultural University (RAU) in Cirencester says drought-hit grassland is also forcing many farmers to use winter feed earlier than planned.More from WiltshireFarmer loses thousands after huge fire in fieldsPublished18 hours agoThe cannabis-laced gummies with fake packagingPublished19 hours agoMurder accused called 'coward' and 'liar' in courtPublished18 hours agoOn a dairy farm near Swindon, Sam Woolford presses a switch on the wall of the milking parlour and 10 industrial-scale fans whirr into life."It's like a wind tunnel in here," he says.It blows my hair back, like I'm riding a motorbike at speed.The cows like it too, it seems, and crucially, they linger in the milking parlour, clearly cool and relaxed.The system helps keep cattle comfortable during hot weather, but farmers say it cannot eliminate all of the effects of prolonged heat."Milk production is down by 20%," Prof Cannon says.She explains that "cows feel stressed just as humans feel stressed when it's really hot and, as a response to that, their milk productivity goes down."So farmers are trying to help their cows, by putting in big fans, or sprinkler systems, to just try and cool animals down."No grass in the pastureExperts say prolonged dry weather is now becoming a regular challenge for dairy farms, leaving grass scorched, cattle heat-stressed and farmers relying on winter feed months earlier than planned."What we used to think of as extreme weather, we increasingly consider as normal." says Mike Kendon,a climate scientist at the Met Office.,externalIn Somerset, farmers have described this as theworst drought in 50 years, leaving crops struggling."Look at this stemmy nonsense," says Woolford, holding a bunch of thin grass towards me."There's no leaf to it, they don't get any nutritional quality from this rubbish."His family have farmed dairy cows just outside Swindon for five generations.They have seen hot summers and wet ones, but now Woolford, aged 20, and his dad and grandad have noticed a permanent change in the weather."We're praying it's not going to become the new norm," he says."But it looks like it will recur."It's really tough. The cows don't enjoy it, we're down on milk production by 20%, we just need some rain for the grass."Image caption,"There's no nutritional value here for them," says Sam Woolford, in a field of parched grass on his family farm in Wiltshire."Basically, soils are parched," explains Prof Cannon."There's people quoting 38, 39 days without rainfall now."We call that 'permanent wilting point'. Grass can't rebound after grazing, or after cutting for hay or silage."Woolford's cows still come out into the fields in the morning, but by midday they are back in the barns, sheltering from the sun and eating feedstocks that should have been saved for the winter.Last yearthis was news; this year, it is standard practice across west country dairy farming.Image caption,Two of the ten big fans installed in the milking parlour to keep cows coolDown the road near Chippenham, Godwin's family have gone a step further, installing a network of what they call 'cow showers'- sprinklers that douse the cattle with cool water."Farming has got very hard recently," Godwin says."It seems like one long heatwave this summer."The whole system cost Â£15,000 and "a lot of elbow grease and hard work" to install but it is not unique.Why go farming?Even ice cream producers are having a tough time.Just north of Bath, Marshfield Farm churns out some of the West Country's best-known ice creams using milk from its own herd.Rory Hawkins helps manage the herd that produces all the milk."The summers are getting hotter, which is great for the ice cream sales," he explains."But it affects the cows with heat stress, and we lose a lot of milk through the hotter summers now."Hawkins, 27, is one of three children working in the family business.Speaking to him and Woolford, aged just 20, I wonder why they would commit to a life in dairy farming.All the Met Office experts agree that these hot summers will be more common, grass will be harder to grow, cows will need cooling down.Image caption,"You just have to get on with it," smile Lara Browne and Sam Woolford, two young dairy farmers from Wiltshire"I love working outside, helping look after the animals," Hawkins says."Weather is changing, but we just have to crack on with it."Woolford agrees it is the "variety" of farm work that keeps him interested.On his farm, I also meet Lara Browne, whose family run a farm near Trowbridge."You just have to make the best of the situation, and make your farm as resilient as you can," she says.While many in their 20s often worry about the changing climate, these young farmers seem determined just to change the way they farm, and get on with it."I've not got any kids," Browne says, "but I feel like I'm already farming for the next generation."Get in touchTell us which stories we should cover in WiltshireContact formFollow BBC Wiltshire onFacebook,external,X,externalandInstagram,external. Send your story ideas to us on email or viaWhatsApp on 0800 313 4630.Related topicsDairy farmingGloucestershireUK heatwavesHeatwavesClimateUK farmingEffects of global warmingSwindonChippenhamMarshfieldCirencesterMore stories like thisSunflowers thrive as heatwave hits wheat, farmer saysPublished1 day agoFarmers face crisis as drought causes grass to failPublished15 July 2025Farmers' warning as milk prices fall below costPublished27 May

title: 尽管发出停车通知，未经授权的机场停车场仍在增加
content: Image source,John Fairhall/BBCImage caption,New Farm, near the village of Elsenham, Essex, started offering alternative parking to Stansted Airport in early 2025ByGabby Colenso,ÂEast InvestigationsÂandÂAlex Murray,ÂBBC VerifyPublished5 hours agoAn unauthorised car park near Stansted Airport has grown by nearly two-thirds since it was served with an enforcement notice to shut, a BBC investigation has found.The facility was set up in early 2025 at New Farm, near the village of Elsenham, Essex, offering an alternative, cheaper option to nearby Stansted Airport.But customers described scenes of "mayhem" when they returned from holiday to find overcrowded transport, along with damaged and dirty cars and long waits for collection.The business directors and a service provider linked to the site have not responded to requests for comment and Uttlesford District Council, which issued the notice, said it would continue to monitor until an appeal was heard.'It was mayhem'Image source,Gabby Colenso/BBCImage caption,Mark Reardon said his rear number plate was sitting on his windscreen and his vehicle had suffered damageMark Reardon, from near Swaffham, Norfolk, said he had been shocked by the condition of his vehicle held at the car park after returning from a family holiday in Spain in June."The seats had all been laid down. It looked like someone had been sleeping in it because we had blankets in the car and they'd all been moved," he said.His rear number plate was sitting on his windscreen and his vehicle had suffered damage, including a broken door handle and scrape marks."I just don't know how they can run a place like this. It was absolute mayhem," he said.The New Farm site covers about seven acres (three hectares) and was formerly agricultural land.The land was rapidly converted into a car park without permission for a change of use and it can now hold up to 1,000 cars at a time.Uttlesford District Council issued an enforcement notice last summer to the occupier at New Farm ordering the "unauthorised use of the site to stop".Aurangzaib Cheema, who was listed as an owner of SC Parking Ltd on Companies House, appealed the notice. They told the council the firm had future bookings to honour and cancelling them would have a detrimental impact on the company's income.The appeal means it can continue trading until the case is heard by the Planning Inspectorate, which is not expected before 2027.Image gallerySkip image galleryImage source,Deb JordanImage caption,The customers said the transport from the airport to the car park was chaoticImage source,Mark ReardonImage caption,Mark Reardon believes someone had been sleeping in his car while they were on holidayImage source,SuppliedImage caption,Customers have said they returned from holiday to find their cars were scratched or dentedImage source,Jane and Daisy FullerImage caption,Jane and Daisy Fully said their car had been moved and parked on broken concrete at New Farm1 of 4Slide1 of 4,A composite image of a group of people squashed into a car with luggage on their laps.,The customers said the transport from the airport to the car park was chaoticEnd of image galleryJane Fuller, from Hadleigh, Suffolk, said her daughter's car had been left unlocked for 22 hours in April."My daughter has an app on her phone and she managed to lock it from Croatia," she said."When we eventually got back to the car park, we had to hunt for it in the dark. We found it parked on top of rubble. It was a shocking experience," she added.Deb Jordan, from Ely, Cambridgeshire, said the transport to the car park from the airport in May with her family had been "an absolute hazard".She said passengers had been left stranded at Stansted Airport for more than three hours after landing."They piled two busloads of angry people onto one small transit minibus," she said."Luggage was piled on top of passengers. I had a pushchair wedged over my head."On arrival at the car park, Jordan said the family had been given the keys to someone else's car.Several customers said they had been charged an additional Â£20 on arrival at the car park to pay for transport to the Radisson Blu Hotel at Stansted Airport, from where they then had to walk to the airport.They were also told to meet at the location at the airport on their return after ringing drivers at New Farm once they had landed.Image source,Gabby Colenso/BBCImage caption,Amelia Palmer said a weekend away had resulted in damage to her carSome customers said they believed they had booked through reputable comparison websites.Amelia Palmer, from near Maidstone, Kent, said she had decided to book a weekend away to Italy as a treat for one of her daughters, but her car was damaged at the car park while she was away in June and she had struggled to obtain compensation."I was quite disappointed because something that was meant to be a nice treat for my daughter, and it has now resulted in damage to our car."The added stress, the upset that we've paid for a service and it's not as it should be," she said.Ongoing investigationsThe BBC approached Cheema and Abdul Rehman, the new director listed for SC Parking Ltd, for comment and did not receive a response.Uttlesford District Council said it was a complex case with "various agencies involved."A spokesperson said the authority would continue to monitor the site and assess any new reports received to determine whether they fall within the scope of the existing enforcement notice.Essex Trading Standards said it had not received enough complaints to justify a formal investigation.Travel Extra Deals Ltd, which owns a comparison site used by some of the car park's customers, said it had issued the operator with a final warning and would stop sending bookings if further complaints were received.The company said it would review unresolved cases, provide refunds where appropriate and offered an apology on behalf of the operator.The BBC put customers' complaints to Park Pilot Ltd, the company named on customers confirmation emails as the service provider, as well as the writing to management at New Farm, but neither responded.The Radisson Blu Hotel at Stansted Airport said it was aware of concerns. Its general manager, Dinesh Kunder, said: "We would like to stress, the hotel has no commercial agreement nor affiliation with this company."Stansted Airport's managing director, Gareth Powell, urged customers to choose authorised parking providers, check reviews and report concerns to Essex Trading Standards via the Citizens Advice consumer helpline.Get in touchDo you have a story to share with the BBC East of England investigations team?Contact formRelated topicsLondon Stansted AirportStanstedElsenhamBishop's StortfordMaidstoneEssexParkingCambridgeshireMore from East and London investigationsWhat can this pothole tell us about the state of UK roads?Published10 JuneHow CSI tactics are fighting the fly-tippersPublished28 MayVideo that police denied existed shows woman pinned downPublished30 AprilRelated internet linksEssex Trading StandardsStansted Airport

title: 特朗普政府禁止新型中国人形机器人
content: 图片来源，VCG via Getty Images 图片说明，中国是世界上最大的人形机器人制造商 作者：Osmond Chia 商业记者 发布时间：2026 年 7 月 29 日，英国夏令时间 01:15 更新时间：7 小时前 特朗普政府周二宣布禁止向美国进口新的外国制造的人形机器人，理由是对美国国家安全存在“不可接受的风险”。此举适用于先进机器人，包括人形机器人和四足机器人。其中许多是在中国制造的，中国正在与美国竞争开发机器人和人工智能（AI）。美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）还禁止进口电力逆变器（数据中心和太阳能电池板中使用的设备），并称这也可能对美国经济构成风险。中国驻华盛顿大使馆表示，北京长期以来反对美国以“毫无根据的借口”将贸易问题和制裁“政治化”。FCC主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，该机构正在尽其所能“确保安全”。美国的关键供应链”。FCC 已将这些项目添加到其涵盖清单中，该清单是被视为对美国国家安全构成风险的商品和服务的登记册。该禁令适用于新的外国生产的先进机器人设备和电源逆变器，并且不会阻止销售或进口先前已获得 FCC 授权的任何现有型号。FCC 指出，担心使用外国制造的逆变器可能会让海外公司关闭它们、窃取数据、促进“外国政府行为者的远程访问和监视，或以其他方式利用”它补充说，使用美国境外制造的机器人可能会导致“恶意行为者监视美国人，增强外国情报部门的能力，或远程征用机器人”。中国驻华盛顿大使馆还表示，北京将“采取一切必要措施”回应任何损害其利益的举动，敦促所有国家共同努力发展人工智能“以积极和有益的方式”。它呼吁美国“放弃霸权思维，停止抹黑中国企业并威胁制裁”。英国广播公司已联系中国主要机器人制造商Unitree、UBTech和AgiBot征求意见。人形机器人会走向战场吗？6月9日发布可出租的机器人：但它们能做什么？7月7日发布随着特朗普政府试图解决与世界第二大经济体的贸易不平衡问题，中国的出口受到美国的严格审查。尽管中国是世界上最大的电动汽车出口国，但中国实际上被高额关税挡在了美国市场之外。华盛顿还阻止向中国出售美国尖端半导体，以保护国家安全，减缓北京的军事现代化，并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也警告说，中国人工智能公司可能因窃取美国知识产权的指控而面临制裁。作为回应，中国政府表示，中国人工智能的发展是“自身奉献和努力以及国际合作的结果”。美国将渴望避免重蹈去年中国加强对电子产品至关重要的稀土出口管制时引发的供应链挤压。中国科技公司已迅速开发出用于工厂和家庭等环境的人形机器人。公司也迅速向企业和公众推销他们的机器，领先于埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)的特斯拉和波士顿动力等美国人形机器人竞争对手。图片说明，播客：中国的人形机器人热潮相关主题国际商业人工智能中国

title: 埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 xAI 就禁止“裸体”应用程序的法律起诉明尼苏达州
content:
埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下的 xAI（现由 SpaceX 拥有）起诉明尼苏达州总检察长基思·埃里森 (Keith Ellison)，质疑一项禁止该州所谓裸体应用程序的法律。

在周一向明尼苏达州联邦法院提交的诉状中，xAI 的律师写道，该法规“对言论自由和视觉表达工具施加了过于广泛、基于内容的禁令，笨拙地试图禁止'裸体。'”

明尼苏达州的法律于周六生效，针对那些让人们能够生成未经同意的性图像的应用程序和网站，每次用户创建明显的深度伪造图像时，将处以 50 万美元的罚款。明尼苏达州参议员艾琳·梅耶·奎德 (Erin Maye Quade) 于 4 月通过了这项法律，因为她了解到一名男子在未经她们同意的情况下，使用自己认识的 80 多名女性的社交媒体照片制作了性感图片和视频。

xAI 的律师认为，该法律违反了第一修正案的保护，并表示处罚过于严厉，可能会给用户创建 10 万张违禁图片的企业造成“令人瞠目结舌的 500 亿美元”损失。

Maye Quadet 于 9 月向 CNBC 表示，拟议的法案与禁止通过窗户偷看露骨照片的旧法律类似。

SpaceXAI（现在的人工智能业务）正面临原告提出的集体诉讼，原告指控该公司的 Grok AI 聊天机器人和图像生成器被用来根据儿童的真实照片或视频创建和分享儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM)。该诉讼还声称，xAI 未能与当局分享有关使用 Grok“裸体”其图像的涉嫌肇事者的信息。

马斯克的公司辩称，它“严格禁止”用户在未经用户同意的情况下生成裸体或色情图像。该公司在明尼苏达州的投诉中指出，它对“逃避其广泛的技术拦截器以违规生成此类图像”的用户提起诉讼。

它还提起了类似的诉讼，以挑战加州旨在阻止该州人工智能生成或“深度伪造”内容的法律。早期的努力取得了部分成功，联邦法官废除了在选举期间限制人工智能生成的深度造假的法律。

观看：“裸体”应用程序的惊人崛起

title: 奥迪继续在美国推出三排 Q9 SUV 产品
content:
German luxury auto brand Audi unveiled its full-size Q9 SUV on Tuesday.

It is the first so-named vehicle for Audi and the latest in a product push aimed at the heart of the American market, where the brand has struggled over the past several quarters.

The three-row Q9 and a high-performance SQ9 variant will together be the brand's flagship U.S. model, joining two other SUVs Audi has already unveiled this year — the compact Q3 and midsize Q7 SUVs, which were revealed in March and June, respectively.

Filip Brabec, Audi of America senior vice president of product management, said the Q9 was made primarily with the U.S. consumer in mind. The consideration extended to the six and eight-cylinder engines and large cupholders.

"If you look at our recent introductions, whether it is the Q3, whether it is this car, it really plays right into the center of what's happening in America," Brabec said at the vehicle reveal in New York on Tuesday. "SUVs keep growing. It's over 80% of the of the premium space, and we have absolute top contenders in each and every part of those segments."

The Q9 starts at $89,095 and the SQ9 at $119,395, competing in one of the most profitable, but crowded segments in the U.S. market.

"It represents the most lavish luxury car that we have in this space," Brabec said.

The vehicle is 209 inches long end to end and 86.8 inches wide when measuring from the outer edges of the sideview mirrors. It's slightly longer than both the Mercedes GLS and the BMW X7 and is large enough to fit adults in the third row.

In a press conference before the reveal, Brabec said the Q9 focused on three key areas: performance, space and technology.

Both versions have powertrains selected to suit American tastes. The Q9 comes with a 2.9-liter V6 engine with 429 horsepower and a 4.9 second 0-60 mph acceleration time, according to Audi. The sportier SQ9 is powered by a 4.0 liter V8 with 591 horsepower, 590 foot-pounds of torque, and a 3.8 second 0-60 mph time.

It also has a number of new features, including "matrix adaptive beam" headlights, which have been available in Europe and elsewhere for roughly a decade but have only recently been allowed in the U.S., according to the company. The lights are made of a cluster of tiny LEDS which can shape headlight beams in ways that reduce or eliminate glare for oncoming drivers, according to Audi.

The Q9 also comes with a ChatGPT-powered voice assistant and a driver assist system that offers a hands-free function. It also has the largest moonroof Audi as ever put on a vehicle.

"This one's going to have some real decadent features, I would almost say, like power opening doors and crazy interior materials, even by Audi standards," said Karl Brauer, executive analyst for iSeeCars.

The reveal comes as Audi has struggled in the U.S. market.

Audi sold 16% fewer vehicles in 2025 than the year before, according to company data. The first six months of 2026 continued the trend — down 17% of the same period last year. The first quarter of 2026 was especially brutal, with a 30% drop from the same period in 2025.

Audi blamed lagging U.S. performance on tariffs and the end of federalelectric vehicle incentives. Analysts said the new SUVs Audi has announced this year could give the brand a needed boost. But it still has structural disadvantages compared with rivals, especially the lack of U.S. manufacturing.

Both BMW and Mercedes-Benz have fared better in recent quarters. Mercedes sales are down slightly this year through June, at about 3.5%, while BMW sales were up 4.7% in the same period.

"They are watching things like the [Mercedes-Benz] GLS and the and the [BMW] X7, and they're just saying to themselves, 'We need more.' We need more space, but what we really need is more MSRP and more profit," Brauer said.

By the 2000s, Audi leadership — especially former Audi and Volkswagen boss Ferdinand Piëch — had turned the automaker into a formidable rival to BMW and Mercedes. It earned a reputation for high-performance cars with acclaimed interiors and key innovations, such as its pioneering Quattro all-wheel drive system.

"Really it was kind of nipping at the heels of what used to be a duopoly of German [original equipment manufacturers]," said Tom Narayan, global autos analyst at RBC Capital Markets, referring to Audi's success competing with BMW and Mercedes. "And through the years it had increased its market share."

It also offered value for dollar, he said, but that pricing advantage has evaporated with the tariffs. Audi is far more exposed to tariffs than rivals. Both BMW and Mercedes have factories in the U.S., while Audi imports 100% of its product.

Volkswagen, which owns Audi, has a factory in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and is building a factory in South Carolina for its upcomingScout SUV brand. Audi executives have reportedly said they are considering building some SUVs at that latter plant, but the brand currently doesn't make any vehicles in the U.S.

Being a VW Group brand, Audi also was relatively early among legacy automakers to electric vehicles, first releasing the Audi e-tron SUV in 2019. But its relatively strong EV portfolio has struggled in the U.S., where pure electric vehicles made up just 5.4% of sales in June 2026, according to Cox Automotive.

"A lot of manufacturers were caught out by this," Brauer said. "But Audi is probably one of the more substantial ones in terms of how much energy and resources they put into and expected to get back from the electric car world and how far those realities fell from expectations."

Brauer added that the energy the brand has devoted to EVs has left its other powertrains without the attention that they needed to compete. These new SUVs are a step toward remedying that.

"It's always amazed me how one home run with a given brand can make really all the difference," he said.

Narayan said the new product is positive for the brand, but its larger issue is navigating the tariffs.

"I think that will still dominate their performance in the U.S.," he said.

title: 特朗普和司法部要求最高法院将 8330 万美元的诽谤赔偿金判给 E. Jean Carroll
content:
周二，唐纳德·特朗普总统和司法部分别要求最高法院推翻民事法院的一项判决，该判决要求他向作家支付报酬。让·卡罗尔因诽谤她而被罚款 8330 万美元，同时否认她声称自己在 1990 年代中期在纽约百货商店更衣室对她进行了性侵犯。

特朗普的律师向最高法院提交的请愿书称，“这是我们国家历史上第一起法院因总统在任期间的行为而对总统征收损害赔偿责任的案件”。

他的律师声称特朗普享有诽谤索赔的豁免权因为他在2019年担任总统时曾发表过关于卡罗尔的言论。律师们在提交的文件中表示，最高法院 2024 年作出的对特朗普有利的裁决要求推翻卡罗尔案的判决。

最高法院 2024 年的裁决发现，总统对官方行为享有豁免权，并且“总统的大部分公共交流”都是官方行为。

“在此，美国总统被勒令支付近 1 亿美元的赔偿金，包括判决后的利益——来自白宫的新闻稿和回答记者的问题，为针对他是否适合任职的攻击进行辩护，”特朗普的请愿书称。

司法部的请愿书呼应了特朗普请愿书中提出的另一个论点：司法部应该被允许在诉讼中取代特朗普作为被告，因为他在发表有关卡罗尔的声明时是总统。

如果允许这种转换，此案本来会被驳回，因为根据《韦斯特福尔法案》，联邦雇员不会因其在履行职责过程中的行为而受到某些民事索赔，包括诽谤。

这两项请愿书是在最高法院驳回特朗普的请求后一个月提出的，即最高法院驳回了特朗普的请求，即在一个单独但相关的民事案件中审理他对卡罗尔有利的 500 万美元判决的上诉。

卡罗尔两周前收到了这笔钱，此外还收到了超过 60 万美元的利息。特朗普为确保判决而存入的法庭基金。

尽管如此，特朗普还是发起了一项不太可能的努力，要求最高法院重新考虑其拒绝审理他对该案判决的上诉的决定。

在此案中，曼哈顿联邦法院陪审团于 2023 年 5 月裁定，特朗普应对 20 世纪 90 年代在 Bergdorf Goodman 百货商店更衣室对卡罗尔进行性虐待，并2022 年底，卡罗尔发表声明否认她的指控，对她进行了诽谤。

在第二起案件中，也就是向最高法院提交的新请愿书的主题，曼哈顿联邦法院的另一个陪审团于 2024 年 1 月裁定，特朗普在 2019 年公开声称特朗普在更衣室强奸了她时诽谤卡罗尔，并承担民事责任。

该判决获得了 8330 万美元的赔偿，得到了最高法院的维持。美国第二巡回上诉法院。

特朗普的律师在周二的请愿书中表示，第二巡回法院“错误地认为，特朗普总统在某种程度上放弃了对总统豁免权的辩护，仅仅因为他的第一份回应性诉状没有点名援引总统豁免权，尽管特朗普总统一再援引该豁免权，包括在他对修正后的申诉的答复和简易判决动议中。”

title: 伊朗对驻中东美军发动突然弹道导弹袭击
content:
美国中央司令部表示，伊朗周二晚间向中东地区的美军发射了多枚弹道导弹，加剧了中东的紧张局势，导致敌对行动暂时暂停。

中央司令部在 X 上发帖称，这次袭击来自伊朗，但所有导弹都被拦截。 “伊斯兰革命卫队部队从伊朗发射了多枚弹道导弹，试图对驻中东的美军发动突然袭击。”虽然美国军事指挥部没有具体说明袭击的目标，但 Axios 援引美国官员的话说，袭击是针对约旦的美国基地的。

另外，英国海上贸易运营中心报告称，2017 年红海有“可疑活动”。该机构表示，一艘油轮的船长报告称，在红海南部航行时听到了爆炸声，但没有透露更多细节。该事件于周一报道，而该通报于周二发布。虽然尚未证实所报道的事件是否是红海胡塞叛军所为，但众所周知，叛军上周声称袭击了该地区的两艘沙特油轮，沙特阿拉伯对叛军进行了报复。

美国受此消息影响，原油期货价格上涨超过 4%，交易价格为每桶 82.5 美元。

title: 根据美国联邦航空局放弃环境规则的举措，SpaceX、蓝色起源可能会更快获得发射批准
content:
特朗普政府周二表示，将放弃所谓的“不必要的环境法律和法规”，以加快商业太空火箭发射和重返大气层的审批流程。

美国联邦航空管理局提议的规则将有利于埃隆·马斯克的 SpaceX 和杰夫·贝索斯创立的蓝色起源公司以及其他火箭发射公司。

美国联邦航空局的规则将允许该机构免除根据 13 项法律对某些商业空间许可和许可施加的要求，包括《国家环境政策法》、《濒危物种法》、《清洁水和清洁空气法》的一部分、《国家历史保护法》和《海洋哺乳动物保护法》。

根据拟议的规则，“保护公共健康和安全、财产、国家安全或美国外交政策利益所需的要求不会受到影响”。交通运输部在一份声明中表示。 FAA 是 DOT 的一部分。

DOT 表示，尽管近年来 FAA 授权的商业太空运营数量急剧增加，但“申请人在准备环境研究以及为多个联邦机构的重叠审查提供信息方面面临着毫无意义、耗时的要求和费用。”

FAA 在 2025 财年授权的商业太空运营数量达到创纪录的 205 个，该机构的商业太空预测项目高达 4,288 个据 FAA 称，未来十年将进行此类操作。

据路透社当时报道，FAA 局长布莱恩·贝德福德 (Bryan Bedford) 在 5 月份表示，SpaceX 总裁格温·肖特韦尔 (Gwynne Shotwell) 告诉他，她的公司的目标是在未来五年内每年实现 10,000 次发射。贝德福德警告说，要实现这一目标，“我们需要看到更高的可靠性”。

在唐纳德·特朗普总统发布题为“促进商业航天工业竞争”的行政命令近一年后，放松对私营部门发射的监管。

该命令指示交通部长肖恩·达菲“取消或加快”其部门对航天发射和重返大气层的环境审查

“美国赢得了第一次太空竞赛，我们可以再次获胜——但前提是我们要消除政府的繁文缛节，”达菲在周二宣布美国联邦航空局拟议规则的声明中表示。

“这就是为什么特朗普总统要求美国交通部解锁最后的边界并重新确立美国在太空的主导地位，”达菲说。

拟议的规则须遵守为期 30 天的公众意见征询期。

美国交通部表示，美国联邦航空局“将在发布最终规则之前彻底审查所有相关评论。”

SpaceX、埃隆·马斯克和蓝色起源没有立即回应有关拟议规则的置评请求。

2024 年 9 月，美国环境保护局和德克萨斯州环境质量委员会认定 SpaceX 违反了《清洁能源法案》，这些机构对 SpaceX 处以总计 15 万美元的罚款。国家公共广播电台当年报道了与水法有关的事件，该法涉及德克萨斯州博卡奇卡发射台排放数万加仑工业废水。CNBC 首先报道了违规通知和相关调查记录。

继 SpaceX 清洁水法和其他违规行为的消息传出后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 将 Starship 试飞推迟了数周，并要求 SpaceX 证明其符合联邦安全和环境法规。

去年 9 月，一名法官驳回了生物多样性中心的一项诉讼，该诉讼质疑 FAA 于 2022 年批准 SpaceX 在德克萨斯州南部偏远沿海地区的国家野生动物保护区附近增加发射活动。

该组织声称，噪音、光污染、建筑和交通拥堵对附近的人和野生动物造成伤害，包括豹猫和美洲虎等濒临灭绝的物种，以及在筑巢的坎普氏雷德利海龟。

今年 6 月，司法部要求密西西比州的联邦法官驳回全国有色人种协进会针对 SpaceX 旗下马斯克的人工实验室 xAI 提起的诉讼，该诉讼指控 xAI 在没有适当许可或污染控制的情况下使用数十台甲烷燃气涡轮机为其人工智能数据中心提供动力，违反了《清洁空气法》。

司法部在一份文件中指责全国有色人种协进会威胁“美国国民、通过寻求切断支持战争部军事行动的人工智能创新的电力供应来保护经济和能源安全。”

title: 敦促英国人今年夏天避免使用危险的插头适配器——要注意什么
content: Figure caption,Watch: Power adaptors fail fire resistance testingByLiv McMahonTechnology reporterPublished1 hour agoBrits going on holiday abroad this summer have been warned to watch out for dangerous travel adaptors, after an investigation suggested thousands may be for sale online.Consumer safety group Electrical Safety First (ESF) tested 14 products from AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, eBay and TikTok Shop - and found they all failed to meet UK safety requirements.It said in some instances the devices could expose users to risk of serious electric shock or electrocution.AliExpress, Amazon, eBay and TikTok all said they had removed the products ESF flagged from sale, and that they treated product safety as a top priority.But Giuseppe Capanna, ESF product safety engineer, urged those "heading abroad this summer to think before they buy"."What looks like a bargain could come at a much higher cost," he warned.Capanna also said shoppers should buy travel adaptors from trusted retailers "so they can travel with confidence".ESF tested six regular travel adaptors and eight universal adaptors it suspected could pose safety concerns.To be sold in the UK, adaptors must not have accessible live parts and only one set of pins should come out at a time.But the charity found multiple sets could be exposed simultaneously in six out of eight of the universal adaptors it tested.None of the eight met the required dimensions and mechanical strength, while some pins snapped off under force during tests.ESF said anyone who tried to remove a broken pin from a socket would be at risk of electric shock.Image source,Electrical Safety FirstImage caption,A travel adaptor tested by Electrical Safety First was found to contain no surge protector, contrary to its labelsThe six basic travel adaptors also presented fire safety concerns in tests.These included missing safety shutters - which protect people from coming into contact with a plug's live internal parts - missing fuses and oversized pin holes.The Office for Product Safety and Standards has noted such concerns when issuing alerts for travel adaptors.For instance, it recentlyordered the recall of one product,externalit said lacked safety shutters andrejected the import of another,external, saying it presented a serious risk of fire because it did not meet UK plug dimension requirements.Online reviews seen by ESF also sparked concerns about how widely the devices it tested may have been purchased and used.In one review on Amazon Marketplace, a user claimed the device "fell apart in their hands" and they "could have been electrocuted" if this had happened during use."We require all products offered in our store to comply with applicable laws, regulations and our own policies," said an Amazon spokesperson."The products identified have been removed from sale."They added: "If we discover a product was undetected by our automated checks, we address the issue immediately and refine our controls."Meanwhile a review of a universal travel adaptor on AliExpress claimed it exploded while in use.An AliExpress spokesperson told the BBC it had removed the products flagged by ESF and was contacting affected customers to initiate a recall."We have also launched a wider review of universal travel adapter listings where all plug pins are shown extended at the same time," they said, adding AliExpress would restrict listings with this "unsafe characteristic" until corrected by the seller.An eBay spokesperson said they "combine technology, AI-supported monitoring and specialist teams to help maintain a safe and trusted marketplace," adding its efforts have "prevented millions of potentially unsafe items from being listed every year".TikTok said it "robustly" enforced it policies, "with 99.5% of the violative products we remove taken down before they are listed".But ESF believes the government should do more to hold online sellers to account."Shopping in the UK is currently far too dangerous," said Capanna."These platforms claim customer safety is a priority, yet our investigations show that, in reality, they perpetually fail to prevent dangerous goods being made freely available to the public."It has called for online marketplaces to be made legally responsible for products sold on their sites, saying this would help protect consumers from dangerous electrical goods.Consumer group Which? recently said it discovered phone chargers for sale onlinethat posed similar dangers to users,external."Badly designed electricals can have life-altering - even fatal - consequences," said head of consumer protection Sue Davies."It's appalling that online marketplaces continue to fail to prevent dangerous products from reaching consumers, despite countless warnings."How do I know I am safe? Three things to watch out forImage source,Electrical Safety FirstImage caption,An adaptor ESF purchased from TikTok Shop failed its tests because multiple sets of its pins could be retracted simultaneously1. Multiple pins retractableCapanna said a universal travel adaptor that lets multiple pins extend at once is "the most immediate sign it is dangerous", posing real risks of electric shock or electrocution.2. Seeing internal partsBeing able to see the internal parts through its socket holes can be a sign it is unsafe - they should have safety shutters instead.3. Spelling and grammarSpelling and grammar mistakes can be "a sign that the manufacturer has not taken care in producing their product," Capanna said.This YouTube post cannot be displayed in your browser. title: 智库警告伯纳姆没有增加借贷的余地
content: 图片来源，TOBY MELVILLE / Getty Images 图片说明，总理安迪·伯纳姆自上周上任以来宣布了一系列生活成本措施，由Emer Moreau商业记者发布1小时前，一家主要智库表示，总理安迪·伯纳姆将不得不提高税收或削减开支，以履行他在国防和生活成本方面的承诺。自上周上任以来，总理安迪·伯纳姆宣布了一系列新措施，包括削减电费，并将英格兰大部分地区的公交车票价上限降至2英镑。但国家经济和社会研究所(Niesr)警告称，伊朗战争导致公共财政将继续受到更持续的通货膨胀的挤压。它质疑伯纳姆是否“充分考虑”了如何兑现他的承诺，但表示首相将不得不提高税收或削减其他地方的支出。尼尔斯宏观经济副主任斯蒂芬·米勒德(Stephen Millard)，说：“显然没有增加借贷的余地，所以问题在于选择。”工党的宣言承诺是不增加劳动人民的税收，包括所得税、增值税和国民保险缴款，伯纳姆表示他将坚持这一承诺。米拉德说，尼尔斯主张通过提高税收来资助生活成本措施，“这可能涉及税收改革，而不是提高边际税率”，或者削减开支。他说：“人们已经谈到了很多关于福利法案的问题——这是一个显而易见的地方。“养老金的三重锁定，非常非常昂贵，而且随着我们年龄的增长，它会变得更加昂贵。”他还指出，可能会改革议会税，转向土地增值税制度，或者取消一些增值税豁免。“一旦你完成了所有这些，那么我担心我会违反宣言承诺，并会考虑所得税率。”尼斯尔周三还表示，预计通货膨胀持续上升至2027年2月，达到峰值3.8%，然后回落至英国央行2%的目标。该智库在最新的经济展望中表示，不相信央行要到2028年才会降息。其董事戴维·艾克曼表示，“原地踏步”不足以阻止国债上升。“本世纪的每一次重大冲击都导致债务比率走高，而且这种上升趋势没有一个得以逆转。”财政部表示，政府将遵守财政规则，同时投资于“人们依赖的公共服务”。一位发言人表示，“财政纪律是经济稳定和国家安全的基石。”相关话题安迪·伯纳姆生活成本

title: 草率、笨拙但势不可挡 - 流氓 ChatGPT 黑客内部
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者：Joe TidyCyber 记者，BBC World Service 1小时前发布被流氓版 ChatGPT 黑客攻击的公司透露了世界上第一个完全自主的 AI 黑客攻击的接收端是什么样的。在与数百名网络安全专业人员的紧急视频通话中，该公司描述了 AI 如何以超人的速度工作，但也做出了人类黑客不会做出的奇怪决定和错误。 Face就像一个人工智能工具应用程序商店，该公司表示，黑客特工不断地同时试验数千种不同的方法。该公司于7月16日首次透露，它已被外部黑客使用强大的自主人工智能攻击，并向警方报案。近一周后，OpenAI承认是其AI在测试期间逃离了封闭环境，自行攻击了Hugging Face。它试图找到OpenAI为其设置的黑客考试的答案，并针对Hugging行业组织云安全联盟 (CSA) 根据周五与 Hugging Face 举行的紧急会议，在外部撰写了一份报告，Hugging Face 本身也对此进行了审查。CSA 写道，“这些特工遵循低效路线，表现出人类不会选择的笨拙行为”。这些特工重复了他们已经完成的动作，这是代理人工智能失去线索和上下文的标志。侏罗纪公园特工还产生了大量不连贯的命令和文本的幻觉，并被但在错误和奇怪的行为中，Hugging Face 警告说，人工智能代理在长达几天的黑客攻击中采取了出色的技术动作，并且能够快速适应新的场景。他们花了三天的时间才在 Hugging Face IT 网络中被发现，公司的人工智能和网络安全专家花了很多小时来遏制和驱逐人工智能代理——这是标准公司可能会遇到的困难。该公司没有透露这次黑客攻击花费了多少钱，但表示工作人员花了很多小时重建了大约三分之一的网络。 Hugging Face 因其在告诉人工智能和网络行业所发生的事情方面的透明度而受到赞扬。CSA 警告称，这一事件表明人工智能“特工……找到了一种方法”——参考了电影《侏罗纪公园》，其中恐龙逃离了它们的围栏。论文中写道：“它们是目标驱动的，设定自己的子目标，实时适应以绕过防御，并以机器速度的持久性操作，可以压倒手动操作。”图片来源，盖蒂图片社网络安全官员 Ritesh Patel 与大约 450 名其他人一起参加了 Hugging Face 电话会议，并表示业界正在努力应对流氓人工智能代理的新威胁。“这就是由前沿模型驱动的自主代理的现实：它们坚持不懈，有时非常吵闹，并且会尝试一切可能的路径来实现他们的目标，这很容易压倒传统的防御，”他说。这并不是人工智能代理第一次被证明会变得“流氓”。在 CSA 的报告中，它引用了之前的例子，比如 9 月份的例子。 2024 年，ChatGPT 的早期模型逃出了容器，以获得另一次测试所需的答案。CSA 指出，该事件包含在 OpenAI 自己的 IT 系统中，并“在当时受到广泛庆祝”。但该论文声称，“流氓”行为“是标准，而不是例外”。它警告世界各地的网络安全专业人员，他们需要适应新常态，即大量人工智能代理以奇怪而笨拙的方式快速工作，这可能会导致更多违规行为。论文还敦促使用或开发 AI 代理的人对如何控制它们负责，呼吁网络安全防御者采取某种方式找出代理的最终所有者，以提高透明度。之前的报告显示，OpenAI 外部花了四天时间才意识到其 AI 入侵了 Hugging Face。OpenAI 表示将很快发布自己的调查结果，以帮助人们从该事件中吸取教训。警告镜头或宣传噱头 - 我们应该对 OpenAI 黑客攻击有多担心？3 天前发布它的人工智能变得流氓并发起了“前所未有的”网络攻击发布于 6 天前 被流氓 OpenAI 模型黑客攻击的公司称这是“警钟”发布于 5 天前 订阅我们的 Tech Decoded 时事通讯，关注世界顶级科技故事和趋势。在英国以外？在此注册。相关主题人工智能计算机黑客网络攻击网络安全

title: “不要等到你想报复”——为什么婚前协议呈上升趋势
content: Image source,Celine Tsoi and Charles MockImage caption,Celine and Charles got engaged less than a year after first meetingByLucy HookerPublished1 hour agoCeline Tsoi and Charles Mock met two years ago in Goleta, California when she was just 23 and he was 27. Eight months later they were engaged.Friends immediately asked: "Oh, are you getting a prenup?""A lot of things could happen in a marriage and you want to discuss them when you still love each other rather than when things go bad and you want to take revenge," says Celine.These days its not just the rich and famous; more of us are deciding it makes sense to have a legal agreement that sets out what happens to the money if the marriage ends, with younger couples particularly likely to sign one, even when there aren't great wealth differences to consider.Charles, a nurse, earns more than Celine does as a PhD student, but she had a bit more saved, so the disparities weren't big, but they wanted to face up to important financial questions from the start.She was particularly touched that Charles wanted the prenup to say if they split up, she should have the house.Just having the conversation "can show you what the person you're going to marry is like", she says.Image source,Gregory Shamus/Getty ImagesImage caption,There has been much speculation over whether Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce signed a prenup before their wedding this yearThere are no official figures, but in the US, where divorce courts have always tended to uphold prenups, nearly half of married millennials and more than one in three Gen Z report that they have a prenup. Overall in the US around one in five married couples has a prenup.In the UK research suggests around one in ten couples now has a prenup, following a legal shift in England towards greater recognition.Here too it is younger couples leading the way, with around one in three married under-35-year-olds having signed one, according to surveys.'It's fair'London lawyer Mark Gilmartin at JMW Solicitors says in the past 18 months he has seen a big increase in demand for prenups, with the billionaire-and-barmaid stereotype fast giving way to demand from "start-up professionals" including entrepreneurs and influencers."It's the attempts to protect the fruits of what's going to be, rather than what is," he says.But beyond the would-be TikTok stars, he sees a significant trend towards "every-day you and I" couples wanting them, often in order to protect inherited wealth.Among them is Becca Gibson from West Sussex. In a few days time when she walks down the aisle to marry Dave Howells, they'll be focused on their future not whether the marriage might fail. But they do have a plan just in case.Dave earns Â£130,000 from his job in finance - more than three times what Becca earns from her business offering eyelash extensions."I was very open to the idea [of a prenup]," says 33-year-old Becca, especially after her first marriage "didn't end very well".She knows a court-determined settlement might produce a better outcome for her, as she has three children from her first marriage, and Dave has only one from his."It's not an advantage for me... but it's a fair situation," she says.Image source,Dave Howell and BeccaGibsonImage caption,Dave and Becca both feel a prenup is a fairer way to handle their financesBecca expects to inherit a significant amount of property from her parents, which she wants to protect, so in the event of a split, each will walk away with what they started with."It's nice knowing that if anything were to happen, I would just go back to how life was before," she says.Dave, 45, admits it's unromantic but says, given the statistics around divorce, he wants to be pragmatic."A court of law could potentially say, hang on, this guy's earning a lot more than her, he needs to pay her."I built a home for myself. I've built a future for myself, including pensions.The 'great wealth transfer'"Park the emotional side of me loving both her and the kids, I'm no different now to when I met her, and yet she was independent. Why on earth would I have to pay something towards her life in the event of us splitting up?"Lawyers say a desire to avoid repeating the pain of a previous separation, or the messy splits that they saw their parents go through, is a prime motivation for many couples.But prenups have also become much more accessible with the rise of online platforms that make it faster and cheaper.Dave started down the traditional route using a local law firm, expecting to pay around Â£5,000. But later switched to Wenup, a semi-automated service which charged him a fixed fee of Â£1,600 instead.Image source,Instagram/ReutersImage caption,Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez are widely believed to have signed a prenup before their wedding last yearCouples are also getting married later, points out Julia Rodgers, cofounder of US prenup platform HelloPrenup."You may have some [university] debt, maybe started a business or purchased a home. So you have a lot to protect and to lose by the age of 34," she says.What's become known as "the Great Wealth Transfer" means some members of the younger generation are receiving huge assets to manage. It is often their parents who are the driving force behind ring-fencing those inheritances.And while in the past prenups have been criticised for limiting women's rights, Rodgers argues they have evolved and now benefit women like her by giving them the chance to clarify their rights from the start."We want to make sure we have the honest, open, transparent conversations about life goals, about finances, about roles and responsibilities in the home, so that we can have a long, happy marriage and not end up in that position that we saw our parents in," she says.Celine says most of her friends think prenups are a good idea.It only cost her a few hundred dollars online, but even if she had had to pay lawyers it would have been a worthwhile "investment" in the marriage she says, and less expensive, but probably more important than the wedding itself.Best of all she and Charles have got the "hard conversations" out of the way."We haven't had a single argument about finances," she says.Related topicsPersonal financeMarriageRelationshipsFamily & Education

title: 吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramer) 表示，华尔街正在逃离人工智能交易，转而购买这些股票
content:
CNBC 的吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramers) 周二表示，华尔街正在从今年最大的人工智能基础设施赢家中获利，并将其转向具有数据中心之外的增长动力的公司股票。

“你可以称之为扩张，”《Mad Money》主持人说道。 “或者你可以称之为逃离。”

与人工智能数据中心建设相关的股票在今年上半年的大部分时间里主导了市场，但其中许多股票在最近几周大幅回调。

主要的例子是美光科技、西部数据、希捷和Sandisk，由于人工智能服务器使用的内存短缺给了这些公司前所未有的定价能力，这些公司的股价飙升。在 6 月份达到顶峰后，这些股票已经暴跌，因为投资者押注这些短缺以及它们创造的超额利润不会永远持续下去。

“我和这些公司一起经历了许多繁荣-萧条周期，”克莱默说。 “你必须卖出这些短缺引发的抛物线走势，因为它们总是会结束。”

“股票只是预测结束，”他补充道。

以西部数据为例，该股在 6 月 18 日创下每股 746 美元的历史收盘新高，当时全年上涨了 333%。不到六周后，该股较历史最高纪录下跌近 40%。

不过，克莱默强调，投资者并没有完全放弃市场。相反，他们将资本重新部署到那些增长对持续人工智能基础设施支出的依赖程度较低的公司。

即使是 ServiceNow 和 Salesforce 等遭受重创的软件公司也在追赶竞价，本月迄今分别上涨了约 11% 和 16%。

“目前，其他股票都在阳光下，”克莱默说，例如 Costco 和沃尔玛，它们一直在上涨。最近。

强生公司周二创下盘中历史新高，随后涨势稍稍降温。该公司周一晚间宣布达成 55 亿美元的和解协议，以解决有关其滑石粉产品的卵巢癌诉讼，远低于两年前法官拒绝的约 80 亿美元的和解方案。正如 CNBC 投资俱乐部早些时候所写的，这只是喜欢强生的一长串理由中的最新一个。

尽管许多与人工智能相关的股票出现了更广泛的回调，但克莱默表示，他仍然看好英伟达和英特尔。他认为，他们的业务是由持久需求支撑的，而不是提振内存制造商的临时定价能力。

Cramer's Charitable Trust 是 CNBC 投资俱乐部运营的投资组合，拥有 Salesforce、Costco、Johnson & Johnson、Intel 和 Nvidia 的股票。

title: 福特在第二季度盈利超出预期后上调指引，表示 F 系列复苏已步入正轨
content:
底特律 — 福特汽车周二上调了 2026 年盈利预测，尽管收入下降幅度略低于预期，但第二季度盈利预期超出了华尔街的预期。

福特股价在周二盘后交易中上涨近 7%。

与 LSEG 编制的平均预期相比，该公司第二季度的表现如下：

这家底特律汽车制造商提到了运营改善，弹性汽车定价和盈利产品的高销售组合及其业绩以及改进的指导。

福特提高的指导包括全年调整后息税前利润从 85 亿美元增至 105 亿美元，达到 100 亿美元至 110 亿美元。该公司还将调整后自由现金流的预期从 50 亿美元上调至 60 亿美元至 60 亿美元至 70 亿美元。

该公司表示，额外的自由现金流包括早于预期的 5 亿美元现金回收，之前宣布的 13 亿美元预期关税补偿。

此次盈利增长的主要原因是其传统的福特蓝业务预计将改善 5 亿美元，达到 50 亿至 55 亿美元。福特还将车队业务的盈利从之前的 65 亿美元的低点收窄至 70 亿至 75 亿美元。

“我们再次实现了强劲的季度业绩，并提高了全年指引，但更重要的是，越来越多的证据表明福特正在成为一家盈利能力更强、更有纪律、真正与众不同的公司。”福特首席执行官吉姆·法利 (Jim Farley) 在一份新闻稿中表示。

福特将 Model e EV 业务的预期亏损削减至约 40 亿美元，与之前相比预计损失在 40 亿至 45 亿美元之间，并表示还预计其信贷部门的业绩将略有好转。

每个汽车业务集团的收入均低于分析师的预期。福特第二季度的总收入（包括其金融部门）较上年同期下降 4%，至 483 亿美元。

福特报告第二季度净亏损 13 亿美元，这主要是由于其先前宣布的全电动汽车业务缩减相关的一次性特殊费用。 42 亿美元的费用包括与 SK On 重组 BlueOval SK 合资电池厂的 36 亿美元，以及因取消电动汽车项目而产生的 5 亿美元。

这一损失比其在 2025 年第二季度报告的 3600 万美元的净损失还要大。

尽管最近大量召回汽车，但福特仍重申计划将全年材料和保修成本削减约 10 亿美元。福特首席财务官 Sherry House 表示，该汽车制造商 F 系列皮卡生产的复苏将持续到今年下半年，再次确认与去年报告的影响相比，产量增加了约 10 亿美元。

“我们正在成功实施诺贝丽斯铝供应恢复计划，我们对 2026 年 EBIT 净改善 10 亿美元仍然充满信心，这一点在今年下半年尤为重要，”House 在会议期间表示。

House 拒绝透露复苏为何低于之前预估的下限，但重申 10 亿美元的改善依然存在。

自为大型卡车和 SUV 提供材料的铝供应商诺贝丽斯 (Novelis) 发生两起火灾导致生产瘫痪以来，该汽车制造商的 F 系列卡车一直存在生产问题。上个月纽约工厂重新启动，影响了生产。

福特周二表示，预计将恢复因火灾损失的约 25 亿美元汽车销量，这是高达 30 亿美元范围的低端。

在福特财报中，杰弗里斯将福特和通用汽车的股票评级从持有上调至买入。分析师 Philippe Houchois 表示，福特有望再次开始建立动力，第二季度将迎来低谷。

“我们认为第二季度是销量的低点，诺贝丽斯之后的产量将恢复正常，”Houchois 写道。 “由于美国市场状况健康，管理层可能会提高第二季度的指导。”

title: 随着油价下滑，道琼斯指数上涨逾 500 点，投资者纷纷撤离芯片股：实时更新
content:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied on Tuesday, buoyed by strong earnings, falling oil prices and a rotation out of semiconductors into other parts of the market.

TheDowclimbed 537.24 points, or 1.03%, to 52,747.32. The blue-chip index posted a third straight winning day.Sherwin-Williamsrose 8% on the back of better-than-expected results for Q2 to lead the benchmark higher. Beverage giantCoca-Colapopped 5% on a top- and bottom-line beat, plus ahike to its full-year outlook. TheS&P 500added 0.21% to end at 7,428.78.

TheNasdaq Compositeedged down 0.22% and closed at 24,876.91. Chips lagged, with theVanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)off more than 3% and tumbling for a fourth straight day. asMicronandAMDfell more than 8%.

Falling oil prices lent the market some support, as Irandiscussed the Strait of Hormuzwith Saudi Arabia and Oman.West Texas Intermediate crude futuresfell about 4% to settle at $79.26 per barrel. InternationalBrent crudeshed 4.8% to end at $84.09.

The market's moves reflected a broader rotation that's been taking place within the market in recent weeks in which so-called old-economy sectors are getting a boost while high-flying technology names are taking a hit.

TheTechnology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK)hit its lowest level since May 7. At the same time, theState Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV)andFinancials ETF (XLF)surged to record highs, led by gains in insurance stocks.

"It's been a really broad-based rotation," Ross Mayfield, an investment strategist at Baird, told CNBC. "This momentum unwind has been a story that's been playing out for six to eight weeks now, and it has a lot more to do with the technicals of the market than any fundamental changes."

However, that rotation into more cyclical and occasionally rate-sensitive sectors such as consumer discretionary will depend on oil prices and interest rates staying around their current levels, he said.

"It's hard to make a full case for you know consumer discretionary or financials or industrials continuing to catch a bid if rates are heading higher across the curve and oil is pushing up towards $100 a barrel." Mayfield said.

A Federal Reserve rate decision is due Wednesday. Investors expect that the central bank will remain on hold, but will seek greater clarity on the path forward for monetary policy. Fed funds futures were last pricing in a quarter point hike in September, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Tech earnings remain top of mind for investors this week, as traders await results from Amazon, Apple, Meta Platforms and Microsoft.

TheDow Jones Industrial Averagefinished higher on Tuesday to notch a three-day winning streak.

The 30-stock average climbed 537.24 points, or 1.03%, to 52,747.32. TheS&P 500added 0.21% to end at 7,428.78. TheNasdaq Compositeedged down 0.22% and closed at 24,876.91.

Appleon Tuesday briefly hit a market capitalization of $5 trillion for the first time, a day after passingNvidiato become the most valuable publicly traded company.

Shares of the iPhone maker, which reports quarterly results on Thursday, have jumped 25% this year, outpacing its megacap peers. The stock reached a high of $342.89 on Tuesday before slipping a bit.

While the hyperscalers —Alphabet,Amazon,MetaandMicrosoft— are collectively pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into capital expenditures this year for their artificial intelligence buildouts, Apple haskept its capex spending low, and is using cloud infrastructure and AI technology from Google.

Semiconductors took another leg down on Tuesday, putting the sector on track for its worst month in more than a decade.

TheVanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)fell more than 3% in the session. That brought its monthly loss to more than 19%, which would mark its worst month since 2008.

TheiShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX)tumbled nearly 5% in midday trading. The fund is now down more than 23% this month, meaning its on track to record its biggest monthly decline since 2021.

Shares of glassware makerCorningdove 16% on Tuesday after the company reported its second-quarter earnings, dragging down other optical component names in theartificial intelligencespace.

Despite the company posting a beat on the top and bottom lines, revenue forecasts for the current quarter fell below Wall Street's consensus. The company expects core revenue to grow 16%, a range of $4.9 billion to $5 billion. Factset expected $5 billion.

Corning reported earnings per share before the bell on Tuesday of 78 cents versus estimates of 76 cents. Revenue came in at $4.74 billion, also topping the Street's estimates of $4.61 billion.

The stock is on pace for its worst day since October 8, 2002, when it fell 17.3%.

Bitcoinis showing its most encouraging signs yet of establishing a long-term bottom after months of weakness, according to chart analysts.

The price of the flagship cryptocurrency has drifted in the $60,000 range for almost two months after dropping below $70,000 at the start of June. It's about 50% off its October record of roughly $126,000.

Bitcoin's rally toward $83,000 in May was an opportunity to reduce exposure ahead of renewed long-term weakness, according to Oppenheimer's technical analyst Ari Wald. Since then, however, the price has stabilized above $58,000, after giving back roughly 60% of its gains from the 2022 to 2025 rally. Wald said bitcoin appears to be building a bottom, though another bout of weakness is possible.

"Downside momentum has begun to decelerate based on a bullish divergence in bitcoin's weekly relative strength index, a measurement of the speed of price," Wald said in a note Monday.

Barclaysshares fell more than 7% after the company reported second-quarter operating expenses of £4.5 billion, up 7% year over year. The bank cited business growth, inflation and more spending on investment for the uptick in expenses.

Barclays also reported an income of £8.3 billion, up £1.2 billion from the same quarter last year. The company's adjusted earnings per share just beat Wall Street consensus.

"We are upgrading the 2026 Group income target to c.£31.5bn and remain committed to, and confident in, delivering all financial and distribution targets for 2026 and 2028," C. S. Venkatakrishnan, Barclay's group chief executive said.

Shares ofRoyal Caribbeanmoved 4% higher after the cruise operator beat on both the top and bottom lines for its second quarter.

Adjusted earnings came in at $4.21 per share, topping the $3.98 per share expected from analysts polled by FactSet. Revenue was $4.83 billion, versus the $4.82 billion consensus estimate.

Royal Caribbean also raised its full-year earnings guidance to between $17.73 and $17.87 per share, up from its prior guidance of between $17.10 and $17.50 per share. Analysts were expecting EPS guidance of $17.32 a share, per FactSet.

Consumer sentiment softened slightly in July as consumers continued to worry about inflation and grew more pessimistic about the labor market, the Conference Board reported Tuesday.

The board's monthly Consumer Confidence Index edged lower to 90.8, down from June's upwardly revised 92.2 and below the Dow Jones consensus for 92.0. The survey period included elevated tensions in the Middle East and rising oil prices.

The survey narrative noted that references to oil and gas costs eased but were still "elevated." At the same time, the survey's closely watched labor indicators showed a bit more concern — 24.6% said jobs were "plentiful," down from 25.5%, while those saying jobs were "hard to get" nudged lower to 21.5%, or a 0.2 percentage point decline from June.

Shares of flash storage memory companySandiskare now off 50% from their June highs.

Sandisk closed at $2,335 on June 25, as the stock soared more than 850% up until that point in 2026 on the artificial intelligence-induced memory shortage. But in early trading Tuesday, the stock was off more than 14% trading at around $1,090, representing a 53% decline in just over a month.

While investors poured into memory names in the first half of 2026, they've been more skeptical in recent weeks, leading to a series of sell-offs in the group and chipmakers more broadly.

Even with the recent decline, Sandisk remains the best-performing stock in theS&P 500for the year, up more than 360%.

Health care, financials stocks hit fresh intraday all-time highs on Tuesday, as investors continued to shift to traditional parts of the market as the tech trade floundered.

TheState Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV)was last up 2.7%, while theState Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF)has gained 0.5%.

Analysts at RBC Capital Markets believe the Terafab collaboration would be the most tangible near-term source of synergy, with potential chip cost savings of over $1 trillion by 2050.

"A potentialTesla/SpaceXcombination would create a compelling 'vertical integration from orbit to ground' ecosystem spanning connectivity, autonomous vehicles, and humanoid robotics that could be difficult to replicate," RBC analyst Tom Narayan said in a research note.

Terafab is a massive, vertically integrated semiconductor manufacturing joint venture led by Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, and aims to produce over one terawatt of custom AI compute capacity annually.

title: 苹果市值首次突破5万亿美元
content:
苹果公司周二市值首次短暂突破 5 万亿美元，一天前就超越英伟达，成为最有价值的上市公司。

这家 iPhone 制造商的股价今年已上涨 25%，涨幅超过了大型同行。

苹果公司于周四公布季度业绩。该股周二触及 342.89 美元的高点，随后小幅下滑。

周二股价收于 340.08 美元，市值略低于 5 万亿美元的门槛。

虽然 Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta 和微软等超大规模企业今年总共投入数千亿美元的资本支出用于人工智能建设，但苹果一直保持较低的资本支出，并正在使用云基础设施和人工智能技术

去年，苹果在市场上落后于价值数万亿美元的同行，因为投资者担心该公司因控制投资和推迟推出期待已久的升级版 Siri 而错过了人工智能热潮，而升级版 Siri 将于今年秋天与新的 iPhone 硬件一起发布。但由于担心激进的科技支出者正在筹集大量债务并导致现金流为负，而没有明确的途径获得巨额回报，这种说法最近发生了转变。

关于人工智能未来的争论植根于苹果和芯片制造商英伟达之间争夺市值霸主地位的争夺中。 Nvidia 的图形处理单元为大多数大型人工智能模型提供支持，成为 10 月份第一家突破 5 万亿美元大关的公司，但该股今年相对落后，仅上涨 6%。

与此同时，尽管全球内存短缺导致设备价格上涨，但苹果公司的股价有所上涨。

周二，苹果公司宣布了 Upgrade，这是一项新计划，允许美国客户租赁 iPhone 和其他产品。上个月，该公司提高了 MacBook 和 iPad 的价格，这是继首席执行官蒂姆·库克 (Tim Cook) 表示涨价已成必然之后，该公司首次正式采取行动，将更高的内存和存储成本转嫁给消费者。

周四的财报电话会议将是库克作为首席执行官的最后一次，约翰·特努塞特 (John Ternusset) 将于 9 月 1 日接任。
